newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says has 250 mln tonnes of marble reserves.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says has 250 mln tonnes of marble reserves.

text.p: Nigeria's marble reserves are more than 250 million tonnes and about 75 million tonnes is proven and ready for exploitation, says the chief executive of the leading marble-producing company in the country.

Garba Bida, general manager of Jakura Marble Industry, told ministry of solid minerals officials who visited his factory in central Lokoja town that the reserves could be exploited for the next 150 years if adequate funds and equipment were provided, the Daily Times newspaper reported on Tuesday.
He said the Nigerian Mining Corporation held substantial shares for the federal government in the company, which has a yearly installed capacity of 500,000 tonnes.

Nigeria's military government says it wants to diversify the nation's oil-dependent economy by exploiting other resources and last year set up the solid minerals ministry to collate data on such minerals and map out strategies for their exploitation.
Its first success was recorded in October when Nigeria resumed exports of coal for the first time since the 1970s by shipping the commodity to The Netherlands.
Garba said his company planned short and medium-term options to shore up its financial base in order to develop and produce marble to meet local demand and for export.
He said the price of a tonne of marble in Nigeria was about 7,000 naira.
